extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset of images densely annotated with region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs, designed to enable cognitive computer vision tasks such as image description and question answering. Contains over 100K images with an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships per image, all canonicalized to WordNet synsets.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.citeAs: Krishna, R., Zhu, Y., Groth, O., Johnson, J., Hata, K., Kravitz, J., Chen, S., Kalantidis, Y., Li, L.-J., Shamma, D. A., Bernstein, M. S., & Fei-Fei, L. (2016). Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation. Approximately 800,000 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) were launched on AMT, where each HIT involved creating descriptions, questions and answers, or region graphs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M (100 million Flickr images) and MS-COCO (328,000 images) datasets. These images are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded onto Flickr by users.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Approximately 6 months of data collection after 15 months of experimentation
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Region descriptions were filtered using BLEU score thresholds (0.7) to ensure diversity. Objects were extracted using Stanford's dependency parser combined with crowdsourcing. Scene graphs were constructed by merging region graph objects with bounding box overlap over union of 0.8. All objects, attributes, and relationships were canonicalized to WordNet synsets. For experiments, attributes were lowercased, lemmatized, and stripped of excess whitespace.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk in multiple stages: (1) Workers drew bounding boxes and wrote region descriptions; (2) Workers extracted objects from descriptions and drew bounding boxes; (3) Workers extracted attributes and relationships to form region graphs; (4) Workers created question-answer pairs (freeform and region-based); (5) All annotations were verified using majority voting (3 workers per annotation, at least 2 must agree) or rapid judgments for objects. Canonicalization of concepts to WordNet synsets was also verified by AMT workers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Majority voting was used for most components: three unique workers voted on each annotation, and an annotation was included if at least two agreed. Rapid judgments were used for object verification. BLEU score thresholds were used to enforce diversity in region descriptions. Canonicalization precision and recall were evaluated on held-out test sets (Objects: 88.0% precision, 98.5% recall; Attributes: 85.7% precision, 95.9% recall; Relationships: 92.9% precision, 88.5% recall).
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 workers per annotation for verification via majority voting; average of 42 region descriptions per image; average of 17 QA pairs per image
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers. Geographic distribution: United States 93.02%, Philippines 1.29%, Kenya 1.13%, India 0.94%, Russia 0.50%, Canada 0.47%, Others 2.65%. Age: majority between 25-34 years old, youngest 18, oldest 68. Gender: 54.15% male, 45.85% female.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford NLP dependency parser (Manning et al., 2014) was used to extract nouns and noun phrases; word2vec (Mikolov et al., 2013) was used for semantic analysis of descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people and towards certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) due to the image source. Workers were predominantly from the United States (93.02%).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. The dataset contains a long-tail distribution of answers. Current models are unable to reason about complex images as shown by low accuracy in region description generation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking computer vision models for: object detection, attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, visual question answering, dense image captioning, semantic image retrieval, image understanding evaluation, and knowledge representation.
